title: Try Magnifier, Narrator and voice access
summary: Find the Accessibility settings and switch Magnifier, Narrator and voice access on and off.

steps.say: Press the Windows key and I together to open Settings.
hints: Hold the Windows logo key, then tap the letter I.
You can also open Start, type Settings, and press Enter.
steps.why: Settings is where Windows keeps almost every option.

steps.say: Click Accessibility in the list on the left.

checks.prompt: Does the Settings page header now read Accessibility?

hints: Accessibility is near the bottom of the left column, above Privacy and security.
Press the Windows key and U to open this page from anywhere.
steps.why: All the built-in helpers for seeing, hearing and interacting are grouped here.

checks.prompt: Does the Settings page header now read Magnifier?

hints: Magnifier is in the Vision group, a few rows down.
Type magnifier in the Find a setting box at the top left.
steps.why: Magnifier enlarges the screen around your pointer.

steps.say: Turn on the Magnifier switch at the top of the page.

checks.prompt: Is the screen now zoomed in, or is the Magnifier toolbar visible?

hints: The switch says Off next to it before you turn it on.
Press the Windows key and the plus key to start Magnifier instantly.
steps.why: Seeing it once helps you decide whether it suits you.

steps.say: Turn Magnifier off by pressing the Windows key and Escape.

checks.prompt: Is the screen back to normal size with no Magnifier toolbar?

hints: Hold the Windows key, then tap Escape at the top left of the keyboard.
Click the close button on the Magnifier toolbar instead.
steps.why: Knowing the off switch makes it safe to experiment.

steps.say: Press Control, the Windows key and Enter together to start Narrator. Press them again to stop it.
hints: Narrator will start speaking. The same three keys turn it off.
You can also find Narrator under Vision on the Accessibility page and use its switch.
steps.why: Narrator reads the screen aloud for people who can't see it well.

steps.say: Go back to Accessibility, then click Speech under Interaction.

checks.prompt: Does the Settings page header now read Speech, with a Voice access option?

hints: Click Accessibility in the breadcrumb at the top, then scroll to the Interaction group.
Type voice access in the Find a setting box.
steps.why: Voice access lives with the other speech options.

steps.say: Turn on the Voice access switch. The first time, Windows downloads a speech model.

checks.prompt: Is the voice access bar now visible at the top of the screen?

hints: The voice access bar appears across the top of the screen when it is running.
On recent builds, press Control, the Windows key and S to toggle it.
steps.why: Voice access lets you control the whole PC by speaking, without the internet.

steps.say: Turn the Voice access switch off again, unless you want to keep it.
hints: Use the same switch on the Speech page.
You can also close the voice access bar with its settings menu.
steps.why: You now know where every helper lives, so you can switch them on when needed.
